hook.line: Mariana asks Tomás to describe the café for her article. A good description has an order: one striking thing first, then the details.
hook.es: Lo primero que llama la atención es el silencio.
hook.en: The first thing that strikes you is the silence.

examples.es: Lo primero que llama la atención es el silencio.
examples.en: The first thing that strikes you is the silence.

examples.es: A primera vista parece un edificio normal.
examples.en: At first sight it looks like an ordinary building.
Seen from outside, it looks abandoned.

examples.es: Visto desde la calle, el café parece pequeño.

examples.en: The first thing that caught my attention was the smell of coffee.

rule:
Start a description with an anchor, then give details, moving from outside to inside.

*Lo primero que llama la atención es...* is "the first thing that strikes you is...". It uses *lo*, not "the first thing" word for word. Change *llama* to *llamó* for a past scene.

*A primera vista* is "at first sight", often followed by a *but*.

*Visto desde afuera / adentro / la calle / arriba* is "seen from...". No "it" is needed: the thing described follows.

The verb after is *parece*: *parece abandonado*, never *se parece*.
smallPrint: Teachers call this focusing the description: a neuter *lo* clause that introduces the first detail.

yourTurn.answer: Lo primero que llama la atención es el silencio.
yourTurn.why: The phrase uses neuter *lo*: *lo primero que*.

pitfalls.wrong: La primera cosa que llama la atención es el silencio.
pitfalls.right: Lo primero que llama la atención es el silencio.
pitfalls.why: Almost. Spanish uses neuter *lo primero*, not "the first thing" word for word.

pitfalls.wrong: En primera vista parece un edificio normal.
